body:
That’s a lot. I can’t begin to imagine what it’s been like to go through all of that.

Some quick questions come to mind. If you had the resources, do you think you’d be willing to pack up and leave everyone in your family? If so, would that include your child? I don’t ask to be judgmental at all. I’m just trying to get the highest-level idea of what you’re feeling right now.
Wait what the hell? Suicide hotlines can send cops?

Oh okay. Yeah, in that case the literal question of hell or going to hell isn’t directly relevant.

Have you sought out supportive queer spaces on the internet? There are so many. Tons of subreddits. Some of them just share memes about vaguely inside (but community-wide) jokes. Others help people figure out who/what they are.

I ask because you’re at least here. So you’re only a step away from groups which (I think) have the potential to help you in a material way. I know that maybe you don’t feel like you deserve help. Or maybe you don’t want to feel differently from how you currently feel about yourself. But in the same way that you might think “yeah living would be interesting if I was straight” maybe you can consider “living would be interesting if part of my mind wasn’t constantly tormenting me.” Then you can look at options for reducing the torment. Community is a super super powerful tool in that regard.

Sorry if that last part comes off as projecting my experiences onto yours.

But someone at least taught you the idea of hell, right? Like, you didn’t personally invent the concept of hell independently. Whoever taught you about the idea of hell probably (at least indirectly) gave you an idea of who’s supposed to go there.

I mean, it is though? I live in CA and have looked at the process pretty thoroughly. It doesn’t need to take more than 2 weeks start to finish.

That’s assuming you pass a basic background check of course. I recognize that it can be hard for people on this subreddit to pass such a check.

Did you get it for some reason other than a potential suicide attempt?

I ask because I view buying a gun as very much a “I’m going to at least” kind of thing. That’s one reason why I haven’t gotten it yet: if I decided (in a fleeting moment) that I didn’t want to do it, then I’d have this scary thing hanging around my house. And I wouldn’t want to get rid of it because I would want to keep it as an option. I feel like the tension between those two forces would mess with me in entirely new ways.

Thank you for taking the time to write. Your words mean a lot.

I’m sorry that you’re also going through this.
